text:
alice: Heads up — canary decks show a sharp 99p latency regression on small-batch inference after the CUDA 13.1 image rolled earlier today. Throughput steady, 99p up ~40%. Blocking further rollout.
ben: Link to dashboards: https://redwood.internal/grafana/d/abc123/smallbatch-99p (canary cluster)
carlos: I pulled a trace with nvprof + triton autotune dump. Kernel chosen for small N changed from matmul_tiled_fast to matmul_generic. autotune table entries look reordered/invalidated.
           ```
           Autotune table (before):
           - matmul_tiled_fast: win for N<=32
           - matmul_large_tile: win for N>32
           Autotune table (after):
           - matmul_generic: selected
           - matmul_large_tile
           ```
diana: Reproducer: `./perf_driver --model llama-mini --device cuda:0 --batch 2 --seq 64 --iters 500 --trace=triton` reproduces 99p spike locally on canary image.
emma: Can we bisect? suspect chain: container base bumped driver->CUDA13.1 and Triton 2.6 landed in same rollout (PRs #4578, #4582). Which landed together in the image build.
ben: Quick run across three images: baseline (driver 12.11) 99p=21ms, image with triton bump only 99p=23ms, image with cuda13.1+triton 99p=30ms. So combo seems worst.
carlos: pprof flame shows matmul_generic doing much more memcpy and lower occupancy. snippet:
           ```
           Flame: matmul_generic ~48% CPU/GPU time
           memcpy H2D ~12%
           kv-prefetch handler ~8% (spikes aligned)
           ```
diana: Timeline trace shows prefetch latency spikes at the same time kernel selection flips. KV cache prefetch tasks queue up and then synchronous slow kernels amplify tail.
ben: triage-bot flagged nightly perf-check: `smallbatch-latency` > threshold, failure id perf-2026-03-18-14:23.
triage-bot: CI: perf regression detected on canary: smallbatch-99p increased by 43% vs baseline.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for service gpu-inference (deploy id canary-2026-03-18-8).
emma: Quick mitigation idea: force kernel hint env var in triton to prefer tiled path for small seqs: `TRITON_KERNEL_HINT=matmul_tiled_fast`. Can we test?
ben: Pushed a debug image with TRITON_KERNEL_HINT applied to staging. Staging numbers: 99p reverted to 22ms, back near baseline. Throughput unchanged.
alice: Good. I'm opening revert PR to back out the triton bump in the canary image while we fix deterministic autotune behavior: PR #4601. Marking rollout as blocked until resolved.
sre-oncall: Received. We'll hold next deploys and open emergency window for revert merge + patch. ETA 60m.
carlos: Root cause hypothesis: Triton's autotune table serialization/order changed in 2.6; combined with CUDA13.1 driver heuristics it causes a hysteresis in selector (stable state flips to generic kernel for small N). Need patch to ensure stable ordering and prefer tiled kernel for N<=32. I'll draft a fix and test.
diana: Also add a perf-ci test: assert kernel selection for common small shapes remains `matmul_tiled_fast` on our reference images.
emma: Owners: Carlos for fix + test, Ben for revert PR review + canary watch, Alice to coordinate gating + customer comms.
carlos: I'll also add more traces to reproduce on M60/A100 flavors; want to ensure not just a hardware interaction.
ben: thumbs up. once revert merges, I'll re-run canary smoke and post results.
ben: (after revert applied) canary status: 99p back to 22ms, canary healthy. Revert PR merged: #4601.
deploy-bot: Deploy completed: canary reverted to image 2026-03-17-19:42.
triage-bot: Follow-up ticket created: INF-9832 "deterministic autotune ordering to avoid kernel selector hysteresis" assigned to carlos.
alice: Thanks all — keeping this thread open until the autotune fix + perf-ci test land. We'll schedule postmortem and timeline for full rollout. :thumbsup:
